rounds.text: The bull case points to strong recent profit growth and attractive valuation multiples [E21, E60], but the fundamental quality of Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri Ltd is undermined by severe cash conversion failures [E34]. Operating cash flow for Mar 2026 stood at just 0.14x of reported profit and only 27% of operating profit, exposing a massive gap between accounting earnings and actual cash generation that strongly suggests acute working capital bloat or aggressive accruals [E34, E37]. This cash disconnect is paired with rising financial leverage as total borrowings expanded to Rs 886 Cr in Mar 2026, pushing the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.05x where total debt exceeds the company's net worth [E38, E39]. Furthermore, historical consistency remains a major structural concern given that the 10-year median return on equity languishes at a meager 9% and the 10-year compounded sales growth is restrained at just 7% [E14, E26]. On the market risk side, the equity carries an extreme historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -93.4% and an annualized volatility of 53.7%, warning that momentum can reverse brutally [E53, E54]. Conceded: the company trades at a low P/E of 9.15x alongside an improving short-term operating margin trend and positive institutional money flow [E1, E33, E44].

While the bear highlights a low cash conversion of 0.14x for Mar 2026 [E34], this must be weighed against actual cash generation including Rs 29 Cr of operating cash flow and Rs 15 Cr of free cash flow in the same period [E35, E36]. Regarding rising leverage with borrowings at Rs 886 Cr and a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.05x [E38, E39], conceded: debt exceeds net worth [E38], but this is offset by surging profitability where TTM profit growth reached 177% and 3-year profit growth stands at 72% [E20, E21]. On the bear's concern over historical consistency citing a 10-year median ROE of 9% and 7% sales growth [E14, E26], the business has structurally accelerated with 5-year sales growth at 19%, 5-year profit growth at 36%, and recent median ROE climbing to 26% [E13, E15, E19, E29]. Finally, while the historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -93.4% and 53.7% volatility reflect past market risks [E53, E54], current momentum is backed by a rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100, a relative-strength rating of 100, and positive institutional money flow [E44, E51, E61].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow reached Rs 29 Cr and Rs 15 Cr respectively in Mar 2026 [E35, E36], but this cash generation is completely overwhelmed by a severe cash conversion ratio of just 0.14x, proving that reported profits are not matching actual cash inflows [E34]. Conceded: TTM profit growth reached 177% [E21], but relying on surging earnings to excuse leverage ignores the reality that borrowings climbed to Rs 886 Cr and the debt-to-equity ratio sits at 1.05x, meaning total debt exceeds the company's entire net worth [E38, E39]. Conceded: 5-year sales and profit growth reached 19% and 36% [E15, E19], but these recent gains cannot erase a long-term track record of sluggish 7% compounded sales growth over 10 years and a mediocre 10-year median ROE of only 9% [E14, E26]. Conceded: the rules-based screen score is 95 out of 100 with a relative strength of 100 [E51, E61], but chasing momentum sitting 91% up the 52-week range ignores the catastrophic historical downside risk of a -93.4% peak-to-trough drawdown and 53.7% annualized volatility [E48, E53, E54].
